newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares end below 4,600 SMI points.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end below 4,600 SMI points.

text.p: 1550 GMT- Swiss shares extended earlier losses to end below the 4,600 point level on the blue-chip Swiss Market Index.
"I think the recent rally is pretty much over," one dealer said. "A level above 4,700 points was probably clearly exaggerated," he added, referring to a March 11 all-time high of 4,734.1.

An easing U.S. dollar and widespread insecurity about the development of U.S. and European interest rates soured sentiment. Volume was below that of the past few sessions and trade was influenced by derivative transactions.
* The SMI fell 79.7 points, or 1.72 percent, to 4,556.5.
* All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) fell 42.02 points, or 1.43 percent, to 2,891.84.
* Shares of Ciba Specialty Chemicals led the actives list. After initially holding up against the weaker market trend, the shares closed with a slump of 5.25 francs, or 4.18 percent, to 120.25.
* Novartis registered shares fell 18 francs to 1,739. The company is due to release its 1996 results on Tuesday. Roche certificates fell 245 francs to 12,190.

* Inspection and testing group Surveillance saw sizeable losses of 150 francs to 3,280. The firm reported a 14 percent 1996 profit increase to 262.7 million francs compared to 230.4 million in 1995. It also increased its dividend.
* Banks were among the major losers of the day. UBS slid 29 francs, or 2.17 percent, to 1,307. CS Group lost 4.75 francs to close at 163,50.
* Industrials Sulzer and Holderbank bucked the trend. Sulzer, which is expected to report on its outlook, rose two francs to 979. The company has already released its 1996 results.
